sentences.text: Brachymylus was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, a group of cartilaginous fish that includes sharks and rays.
This extinct genus belongs to the family Callorhinchidae, which contains the modern plough-nose chimaeras known for their distinctive snouts.
The genus was first described by Woodward in 1892.
Currently, only a single fossil occurrence of Brachymylus has been recorded in scientific databases.
The animal lived during the Pliensbachian stage, a time period spanning from 192.9 to 184.2 million years ago.
